"''That's my line.|Riot Mar and Din Djarin|audio=RiotMarMandalorian-TMS01CH05.flac|}} '''Riot Mar''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[bounty hunter]] working for the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild]]. In [[9 ABY]], he attempted to capture the [[bounty]] known as [[Din Grogu|Grogu]] by pursuing the [[Mandalorian]] [[Din Djarin]], a bounty [[Hunting|hunter]] who had [[Incident on Nevarro|betrayed]] the Guild, in his own customized [[Helix J-104 starfighter]]. Mar managed to track down the Mandalorian in [[Realspace|space]] above the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]] and attacked his [[ST-70 assault ship|gunship]], the ''[[Razor Crest]]''; however, Djarin [[Death|killed]] him, destroying his [[Riot Mar's starfighter|fighter]] during the battle. ==Biography== {{Quote|Hand over the child, Mando.|Riot Mar, to Din Djarin|}} Riot Mar worked as a [[bounty hunter]] as a member of the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild]] during the [[New Republic Era|time]] of the [[New Republic]]. In [[9 ABY]], following a [[Incident on Nevarro|fight]] on the [[planet]] [[Nevarro]] in which the [[Mandalorian]] [[Din Djarin]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 8: Redemption}} had betrayed the Guild and fled with a [[bounty]], the [[Youngling|infant]] [[Din Grogu|Grogu]],{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 13: The Jedi}} Mar attempted to recapture the child from the Mandalorian, considering him a lucrative target.{{EncyclopediaCite|Post-Galactic Civil War and the Mandalorian}} [[Pilot]]ing his own [[Riot Mar's starfighter|starfighter]], a customized [[Helix J-104 starfighter]],''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' the bounty [[Hunting|hunter]] engaged the Djarin's [[ST-70 assault ship|gunship]], the ''[[Razor Crest]]'', in [[Realspace|space]] above the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]], managing to tail behind the traitor and fire upon him. Getting closer to the ''Razor Crest'', Mar demanded that Grogu be handed over, offering to spare the infant's life and later suggesting he would spare Djarin's. [[File:Riot_Mar_Death.png|thumb|left|300px|Riot Mar was killed by Din Djarin.]] Damaging the [[gunship]]'s left [[engine]], Mar believed he had his target trapped. The pilot continued firing while spinning his [[Starfighter|vessel]] as he pursued the ''Crest'', landing several hits on the latter. Djarin then spun the ''Razor Crest'' but was unable to shake the bounty hunter; however, the Mandalorian then quickly slowed the gunship. Taken by surprise, Mar narrowly avoided crashing into the ''Razor Crest'', catching a wing on one of its engines, but was [[Death|killed]] as Djarin opened fire on the bounty hunter's [[Starship|vessel]] and destroyed it. Mar's final scream sounded through the ''Crest''{{'s}} [[Comm unit|comm]] at that moment.[[The Mandalorian Junior Novel|''The Mandalorian'' Junior Novel]] As a result of the skirmish, the ''Razor Crest'' suffered a number of damages, including a [[fuel]] leak that Djarin later fixed on Tatooine. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|I might let you live.|Riot Mar, to Din Djarin|}} Riot Mar was a 1.93–[[meter]]–tall (6 [[Foot|feet]], 4 inches) [[human]] male with light skin, [[Color|gray]] [[hair]], and gray [[eye]]s. Although he would show mercy on his targets if it helped him capture them, he had a chance of shooting them regardless if it made the hunt easier for him. When demanding that Din Djarin hand over Grogu, he suggested he might even spare the Mandalorian if he complied. He made a cocky and overconfident impression on Djarin, gaining a false sense of security after dealing blows to the ''Razor Crest''. Mar sometimes overestimated his abilities and survival prowess due to his ego. ==Skills and abilities== [[File:Riot_Mar_Ship.png|thumb|right|280px|Riot Mar pursued the ''Razor Crest'' in his fighter.]] Mar was an expert tracker and an experienced pilot skilled in shooting and hunting. However, he was outsmarted in [[Space warfare|ship-to-ship]] combat by Djarin, despite having a more maneuverable ship. ==Equipment== Mar wore a yellow pressurized [[Environment suit|g-suit]] that included a [[life support]] unit, which had an air supply hose protruding to his black [[breath mask]] decorated with a pattern of white predatory [[Tooth|teeth]]. He also wore brown [[Clothing|pants]], [[glove]]s, a [[belt]], a white [[helmet]] with a yellow blast shield, also with a white teeth pattern, and red earphones. Mar flew a customized Helix J-104 starfighter outfitted with technology to make it suitable for ship-to-ship combat. The craft was nimble and more maneuverable than the ''Razor Crest''. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|They described Riot Mar as having a crazy exotic helmet and a lot of aviation-style patches. It seemed to me like he's like a decorated Top Gun pilot.|Brian Matyas|[[The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian (Season One)|''The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season One]]}} [[File:Riot-Mar-Concept-Art.png|thumb|left|300px|Concept art for Riot Mar in his fighter by Ryan Church and Brian Matyas]] Riot Mar first appeared in "[[Chapter 5: The Gunslinger]]," the fifth episode of the [[The Mandalorian Season One|first season]] of the [[Disney+]] television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'' that aired on [[December 6]], [[2019]].{{InsiderCite|201|Star Wars: The Mandalorian Season One Companion|''Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season One Companion}} He was portrayed by [[Rio Hackford]], who also provided the motion-capture work for the [[IG-series assassin droid]] [[IG-11]] in the show.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 1: The Mandalorian}} Concept art for Mar was done primarily by artist [[Brian Matyas]], while fellow artist [[Ryan Church]] contributed to much of the conception of Mar's fighter. Being given a description of Mar, a crazy exotic style helmet and a bunch of aviation patches, Matyas pictured a decorated pilot from the [[1986]] film{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/ghostbusters-top-gun-enter-national-849092|text='Ghostbusters,' 'Top Gun,' 'Shawshank' Enter National Film Registry|author=Mike Barnes|date=2015-12-16|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|The Hollywood Reporter]]|archivedate=20190408142727}} [[Wikipedia:Top Gun|''Top Gun'']] and looked into garments from the [[Wikipedia:Cold War|Cold War]] era. Matyas's first version of Mar resembled a [[Wikipedia:World War II|World War II]] pilot to him. The artist was also asked to provide intimidating shape language to the bounty hunter, which led to another version of Mar to remind him of an [[W:c:lotr:Uruk-hai|Uruk'hai]] from the [[Wikipedia:The Lord of the Rings|''Lord of the Rings'']] franchise. In another version, Matyas took inspiration from a [[Imperial Starfighter Pilot|TIE fighter pilot]] and the character [[Boba Fett]], although the [[armor]] in the end product looked too expensive for a character who would not last long. He also made a dozen designs of toothy [[mouth]]s, trying to merge it onto a respirator design. Art director [[Doug Chiang]] suggested putting the mouth where the muzzle met the visor, which Matyas liked; he considered the idea similar to the teeth designs on the noses of [[Wikipedia:Bomber|bombers]]. [[File:RiotMarBTS-DGTM5.png|thumb|right|300px|Rio Hackford filming in the cockpit of Riot Mar's starfighter.]] Filming for "Chapter 5: The Gunslinger" took place between [[January 9]] and [[February 12]], 2019. The shots of Mar inside his fighter were filmed with only a half-built cockpit and an [[Wikipedia:Light-emitting diode|LED]] screen behind it to visualize the changing position of realspace around Mar's fighter while it maneuvered.{{DisneyGallery|Practical}} In [[Joe Schreiber]]'s [[2021]] [[The Mandalorian Junior Novel|junior novelization]] of ''The Mandalorian'' Season One, Mar's two lines "Hand over the child, Mando." and "I might let you live." from the episode were merged into a single sentence. This article presents his dialogue as depicted in "Chapter 5: The Gunslinger." ==Appearances== *[[The Mandalorian Junior Novel|''The Mandalorian'' Junior Novel]] {{Ab|The Mandalorian Junior Novel (audiobook)}} *[[The Mandalorian – The Graphic Novel of Season 1|''The Mandalorian'' – The Graphic Novel of Season 1]] {{Voice}} *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 5: The Gunslinger}} {{1st}} *[[The Mandalorian 5|''The Mandalorian'' 5]] *[[The Mandalorian 6|''The Mandalorian'' 6]] {{C|Indirectly mentioned only; in the opening crawl}} ==Sources== *{{DisneyGallery|Practical}} *{{SW|url=series/the-mandalorian/chapter-5-guide|text="The Gunslinger" Episode Guide | The Mandalorian}} *{{InsiderCite|198|Jedi Master's Quiz}} *[[The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian (Season One)|''The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season One]] *{{SW|url=news/lego-star-wars-advent-calendar-2021|text=Mando Brings the Holiday Cheer with This Year's LEGO ''Star Wars'' Advent Calendar - Exclusive Reveal}} *{{EncyclopediaCite|Din Djarin and Other Characters of the Underworld}} *{{LEGOCite|num=75307|name=LEGO Star Wars Advent Calendar}} {{C|Starfighter only}} *''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' *''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian Handbook]]'' *{{EncyclopediaCite|Post-Galactic Civil War and the Mandalorian}} *''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' {{Imo}} *''[[The Mandalorian: The Adventures of Din Djarin]]'' *[[Star Wars Starships & Vehicles 84|''Star Wars Starships & Vehicles'' 84]] *''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' *{{Databank|riot-mar|Riot Mar}} ==Notes and references== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Riot Mar}} {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |de=Riot Mar |es=Riot Mar |fr=Riot Mar |ja=ライオット・マー |ka=რიოტ მარი |nl=Riot Mar |pl=Riot Mar }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Mar, Riot}} [[Category:Bounty Hunters' Guild bounty hunters]] [[Category:Humans]] [[Category:Individuals with he/him pronouns]] [[Category:Males]]
